nodes.description: Biallelic nonsense, frameshift and canonical splice-site variants truncate CWC27. Patient blood RNA and mouse retina show that the mutant transcripts escape complete nonsense-mediated decay, so truncated protein may persist. CWC27 binds CWC22 directly through its C-terminal region, forming a heterodimer that sits in the Bact spliceosome and stabilizes eIF4A3 binding; the protein binding term records that shown interaction. No peptidyl-prolyl isomerase activity term is bound, because the human cyclophilin domain lacks a conserved active-site residue and is described as catalytically inactive. Allele position predicts severity: C-terminal truncations such as p.Val335Serfs*13 cause retina-restricted disease, while earlier truncations cause the syndromic form.

nodes.description: Complete loss of Cwc27 in knockout mice (tm1b, tm1Lex) causes near-complete embryonic lethality, growth retardation, neural tube closure failure, absent limb buds and delayed digit separation. These are much more severe than the human syndrome but point to a developmental requirement for CWC27 that the hypomorphic retinal mouse does not show. Whether mis-splicing in neural crest, limb or brain precursors is the operative step has not been shown, so this node is linked to the variant node without a mis-splicing intermediate, and the neurodevelopmental features are attached to it without a known mechanism.

nodes.description: Photoreceptors degenerate, with loss of the outer nuclear layer and outer segments in patients. In mice the evidence comes from the hypomorphic K338fs model, whose degeneration is driven mainly by photoreceptor death, includes cones, and is reduced by AAV8 delivery of Cwc27 to photoreceptors. Whether the retinal pigment epithelium fails independently has not been studied.

nodes.description: Evidence comes from the Cwc27 K338fs/K338fs mouse retina, where bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing found altered splice-site usage and intron retention alongside gene expression changes, the first in vivo evidence that CWC27 acts as a splicing factor. In a human RPE cell line (hTERT RPE-1), CWC27 knock-down changed expression of many of the same genes as CWC22 knock-down. Which mis-spliced transcripts explain photoreceptor loss is not established.
